title: Development versus production
runtime: React 19.3 learning project with a current Vite setup. Version-specific commands must be checked against the linked React, Vite, and npm pages before use.

objectives.text: Explain the purpose of development mode.
Explain what a production build creates.
Use preview for a local production check.

learningFlow: Trace or change a practical example
Apply it in a fresh project decision
Review after two and seven days

diagnostic.question: What problem does development versus production help you solve?
diagnostic.answer: Name the relevant layer, its input and output, and one problem it does not solve.

sections.title: Development optimizes feedback
sections.body: The Vite development server prioritizes fast startup, useful source errors, module serving, and hot updates. React development checks can intentionally do extra work to reveal unsafe assumptions. Development output is for local iteration and contains behavior or metadata that should not define production performance.

sections.title: Build produces deployable assets
sections.body: npm run build makes a production bundle, using index.html as the default entry and writing optimized assets to dist by default. It resolves and transforms modules, splits or bundles code, rewrites asset references, and removes development-only paths where supported. A successful build proves compilation, not correct product behavior.

sections.title: Preview serves the built output
sections.body: npm run preview serves the files already produced in dist. It helps catch missing assets, wrong base paths, and behavior that differs from the development server. Preview is a local check, not a production hosting platform, security review, load test, or deployment. Rebuild after source changes before trusting preview.

sections.title: A build is not online yet
sections.body: Deployment copies or releases built assets to a real host and configures URLs, caching, HTTPS, environment values, and route fallbacks. Apps hosted below a subpath may need Vite’s base setting so generated asset URLs are correct. Test direct navigation and reload behavior on the actual host because a client router and a file server have different responsibilities.

sections.title: Use evidence instead of setup guesses
sections.body: When setup fails, identify the layer before changing code. Read the terminal command and first error, confirm the current directory and versions, check the browser Network and Console, and trace the entry file to the root component. Make one small correction, rerun the same check, and record what proved the fix.

interviewQuestions.question: What responsibility does development versus production have in a React project?
interviewQuestions.answer: Explain the purpose of development mode. Explain what a production build creates. Use preview for a local production check. Distinguish building from deployment.
interviewQuestions.followUp: What important responsibility belongs to another layer?

interviewQuestions.question: How would you debug a failure related to development versus production?
interviewQuestions.answer: Reproduce the smallest failure, confirm the current directory and versions when relevant, read the first terminal or browser error, trace the entry and root, and test one hypothesis at a time.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which evidence would make you change layers?

interviewQuestions.question: Which tradeoff in development versus production should a team decide explicitly?
interviewQuestions.answer: The team should match tools and boundaries to product needs, record version and deployment assumptions, and avoid treating a starter template as a complete production architecture.
interviewQuestions.followUp: How could the answer change for an existing server-rendered site?

mastery.policy: Reading commands or following the guided project is not mastery. Recreate the setup without copying, explain every tool boundary, diagnose one failure, and verify a production build.

problems.prompt: Invent one setup failure and diagnose it by evidence.

problems.prompt: Teach development versus production to a learner without using unexplained tool names.

problems.solution: The choice should follow stated requirements and include a verification plan.

commonMistakes.symptom: Every setup problem is described as a React error.
commonMistakes.cause: Browser, Node, npm, Vite, project files, and React responsibilities were mixed together.
commonMistakes.fix: Identify the failing layer from the command, URL, stack, file, or tool panel before editing.

commonMistakes.symptom: Commands work in one terminal but fail in another folder.
commonMistakes.cause: The current directory or active Node installation differs.
commonMistakes.fix: Check the path, package.json, lockfile, node -v, and npm -v in the same terminal.

commonMistakes.symptom: The starter template is treated as a complete production plan.
commonMistakes.cause: Scaffolding and build features were confused with routing, data, server, security, and deployment architecture.
commonMistakes.fix: Write product requirements and assign each responsibility to React, a build tool, a framework, the platform, or backend code.

publicationChecklist.note: Concept-complete setup draft. Recheck version-specific commands, run broader browser behavior checks, obtain independent review, and complete a learner trial before publication.
